newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - May 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - May 21.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In findings which have been described by Australian Institute of Superannuation Trustees as "rather harsh", a survey by Coopers & Lybrand has found mistakes by superannuation trustees are costing their members about A$2 billion a year in lost earnings, wih investors missing out on the earnings because their trustees are choosing the wrong funds managers to handle their super savings. Page 1.

Amid a consensus among leading food analysts that Burns, Philp & Co was looking at a A$300 million shortfall on the book value of the sale of its herbs and spices divisions, shares in the company fell 20 cents yesterday, recovering later to close nine cents lower at A$1.87. The negative market result follows Burns & Philp's announcement on Monday of a major board shake-up. Page 23.

Speaking after Orogen Minerals' annual meeting in Port Moresby yesterday, managing director Charles Lepani revealed that Chevron, the leader of the Papua New Guinea gas pipeline project, had recently met with Comalco Ltd to try and persuade the group to use gas from the pipeline for its A$1 billion aluminium refinery, which may be built in Gladstone in Queensland. Page 23.

In a move designed to slash about A$5 million from annual operating costs in the first stage of a major review of the troubled Telfer mine in Western Australia, Newcrest's new managing director Ian Johnson has announced 126 people will be sacked from the project, about 25 per cent of the company's total workforce at Telfer. Page 23.

Thanks largely to an expected A$3 million abnormal gain from the sale of equities during the year, Perpetual Trustees Australia Ltd has forecast a 20 per cent rise in net profit for the financial year ending June 30 and a two cent increase in final divided. The company expects to report a A$17.5 million net profit for the 12 months, compared to A$14.6 million in the previous financial year. Page 25.

Shares in Alan Jackson's textile and plant hire group Austrim Ltd leaped to a record A$2.89 yesterday, largely due to recent acquisitions. The company is expecting a strong earnings performance in the current half-year, well-ahead of the record first-halfresult. Page 25.
THE AUSTRALIAN

In a move which would generate additional funds required for Optus Communications to finance 100 per cent of the loss-making Optus Vision business which it acquired in late March, Optus directors are considering doubling the capital raising component of the group's upcoming float to about A$800 million. Page 21.

According to sales figures released yesterday by Wool International, there has been a 17 per cent increase in wool exports for the first nine months of 1996-97. The strong result was underpinned by a surge in sales to China, Australia's biggest wool market, and positive sales to Italy and Taiwan, our next two most important markets. Page 21.

Under a review of marketing strategy initiated by new chief executive Peter Wilkinson, upmarket retailer David Jones Ltd will dump its Dalmation dog corporate branding campaign after research found men did not understand the concept and while women liked the ads, they were not inspired to visit the stores. The review may also see the company reconsidering its advertising agency arrangements. Page 21.

In a poor result which comes after Standard & Poor's placed the group on creditwatch negative after its decision to sell its herb and spice businesses in Europe and North America, Burns Philp & Co Ltd shares slipped nine cents yesterday to A$1.87 as investors expressed disquiet with the sale. Page 23.

Speaking at Plutonic Mining Ltd's annual meeting in Sydney yesterday, chairman Paul McClintoch forecast the sale of the group's secondary assets, a move that could raise about A$100 million. McClintoch said Plutonic will be giving serious thought to its operations and structures following the Centenary discovery in Western Australia, which saw its gold resource in April revised upwards to 2.1 million ounces. Page 23.

In a submission to the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission, the National Farmers Federation says the proposed takeover of the Bank of Melbourne by Westpac would exacerbate the lack of retail competition in the non-mortgage banking market. The NFF goes on to describe the retail banking sector as a "highly concentrated oligopoly". Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Following years of uncertainty about two of its key privatisations, the Federal Government is on track to meet its June 30 deadline for the A$650 million sale of its 18,000-strong vehicle fleet, DASfleet, and investment bank AIDC, which is tipped to fetch only about A$250 million despite a bid from at least one foreign bank. Page 29.

After being placed on credit-watch negative by ratings agency Standard and Poor's amid concerns that the likely sale price of its spices and herbs businesses and the resulting writedowns might lead to a breach of its bank loan covenants, Burns, Philp & Co yesterday met bankers to reassure them of the impact of the sale on its debt levels. Page 29.

Less than a week after Newcrest Mining's former boss, John Quinn, resigned after 27 years with the company, new acting chief executive Ian Johnson has announced that 126 workers at the Telfer gold mine in Western Australia and its Perth support office wil be retrenched in a bid to boost earnings from the project. Page 29.

According to a Coopers and Lybrand Securities survey of 151 super funds investing in either balanced or specialist funds, most superannuation funds choosing specialist fund managers over the past four years instead of balanced fund managers have been disappointed. Page 31.

Following the announcement earlier this month that Imperial Chemical Industries would sell its A$2.1 billion stake in its Australian offshoot to help fund the purchase of Unilever's speciality chemicals division, ICI Australia could outlay up to A$220 milion on a buyback of its shares, with the company's board expected to make a decision next week. Page 31.

According to a KPMG survey designed to review the impact of the Australian Stock Exchange's decision last year to introduce a listing rule requiring all listed companies to include a statement in their annual reports on their main corporate governance practices, less than a fifth of top companies had a documented procedure to review their board's performance. Page 31.
THE AGE

The Australian Business Chamber has expressed concern over Federal Government plans to keep the details of a car industry report, which looks at the level of car tariffs after the year 2000, secret until after its viewing by Cabinet. They want the report to be released next week, after it is presented to Parliament, as is normal practice. Page B1.

The telecommunicatoions industry is facing a period of turmoil after its deregulation on July 1, with Optus Communications chief Ziggy Switkowski has warning of volatile profits in the next couple of years. He said telephone revenue would underpin the company's revenue in the next few years. Page B1.

A regional summit concentrating on Asia and organised by the World Economic Forum, will be held in Melbourne in the year 2000. The summit is expected to attract regional heads of state and government officials, and it has been supported by the Business Council of Australia. Page B1.

Market exultation over the decision by Burns Philp to quit the herbs and spices trade was short lived with the company closing down nine cents yesterday, with 2.8 million shares traded. Burns rose 11 cents in optimism last week with the decision to quit herbs and spices, and with the resignation of managing director Ian Clarke. Page B2.

The Commercial Economic Advisory Services of Australia has released the results of a survey showing direct marketing, such as telephone sales and junk mail, are growing faster than more traditional forms of advertising. The survey, which traced the amount spent on direct marketing, showed an increase in expenditure of 14.5 per cent. Page B3.

Newcrest mining is to sack 126 people, comprising of 87 award workers and 39 staff, in a bid to return the company to economic health. The job losses will cover non-core service and maintenance functions that will be given to outside contractors in the future. Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
